text:
Devon: quick idea: a "donation-backed" path where cold host pages can be temporarily repurposed as GPU backing for very small allocations (kv-cache slots, tiny embeddings) to avoid PCIe copy on the hot path.
Linh: sketch the happy-path? feels like correctness landmines if reclaimed mid-run.
Devon: happy-path: allocator probes a can-donate callback; if a host page is marked cold and tenant allows donation, map+pin it and expose to GPU as host-backed. allocation gets ALLOC_DONATED flag. reclaim path kicks the moment the donor page becomes hot again.
Alex: how does this differ from staging pool? we already have reserved host buffers to avoid copies.
Devon: staging assumes reserved runway and extra host memory. donation reuses existing tenant-owned host pages (no extra reserved pool). it's ephemeral — not a replacement for staging, more of a low-cost optimization for tiny short-lived work.
Maria: reclaim semantics? if OS/tenant needs the page back while an inference uses it, what's the contract?
Devon: three policy outcomes per-alloc: 1) migrate-to-staging async (best-effort), 2) force-sync migrate (blocking; fall back to copying to device if necessary), 3) allocation-time opt-out (strict tenants). Exposed as config: donation_mode = [off, soft, strict]; donation_grace_ms; donation_max_bytes.
Sam: we need per-tenant quotas so noisy neighbors can't lose pages silently.
Devon: plan: per-tenant donate_credits + global donor_pressure throttle. credits consumed by active donated bytes; replenished on activity. donate_credits also visible in console.
Linh: telemetry list: donation_hit_rate, donation_reclaim_latency_ms, donation_failed_reclaims, donation_fallback_count, p99_tail_spike_on_reclaim.
Alex: fragmentation concern: scattering donated pages increases allocator complexity and compaction cost.
Devon: donation will prefer same-arena runs; small donations coalesced into donated-slabs. background compactor prefers reclaiming donated-slabs to reduce churn. also prefer run-length >N pages for donation to minimize scatter.
Maria: kernel concerns: we must pin host pages for GPU mappings; that has cost. batching and short TTLs to amortize. also pin/unpin metrics.
infra-bot: deploy-note: feature-flag + safety-watchdog required for hosted rollout.
Devon: rollout plan: Dedicated -> Private -> Hosted opt-in. gated by feature flag + RBAC + telemetry check.
Alex: correctness & snapshotting: donated pages must be excluded from checkpoint/mtable snapshots. need alloc flags (ALLOC_DONATABLE, ALLOC_NO_CHECKPOINT).
Sam: failure modes: reclaim latencies causing inference p99 spikes. need a global emergency kill-switch to fall back to staging copies.
Linh: implementation roadmap: 1) allocator probe + credit accounting, 2) donate mapping + pin/unpin, 3) reclaim hook in evictor with three outcomes, 4) compaction/telemetry, 5) perf harness.
Devon: perf microbench: 1000 small allocations/sec (4KB-64KB) compare: donation=on/off, staging-reserved baseline, measure p50/p95/p99 and PCIe copy counts.
Maria: pack the state machine diagram into RFC: states = host-owned -> donated (mapped/pinned) -> in-use-by-gpu -> reclaiming -> migrated/staged/evicted -> host-owned. include invariants about who owns mapping and when pin is released.
Alex: add a fast-path probe in hot alloc path that cost-tests can-donate with a simple heuristics (recent-access histogram threshold).
Devon: security note: ensure KMS/HSM keys unaffected; donations only for non-persistent caches.
Commander: +1. Devon, open a short RFC w/ API knobs, state machine, telemetry, quota model, and a perf plan. link the RFC here and tag reviewers.
Devon: will do. target: RFC by Tue EOD, prototype branch within 2 weeks, perf harness + dashboard. cc @Maria @Linh @Sam for reviews. :rocket:
